chunk-001:c002.proposition: Inductive evidence for efficient causes equally supports the principle that whatever has an efficient cause of its existence also has a material cause, so induction alone cannot justify retaining one principle while rejecting the other.

orphanFallback.rationale: Independently of a retained opposing move, the empirical parity between efficient and material causation supplies a constructive reason to withhold an inference to creation without prior matter.

chunk-001:c003.proposition: Observed causation occurs within spacetime, so its evidential scope is physical rather than metaphysical and does not by itself extend to the totality of time and space.

orphanFallback.rationale: Even without an earlier retained opposing move, distinguishing physical evidence from metaphysical scope constructively limits what ordinary causal experience warrants about the universe as a whole.

chunk-001:c005.proposition: Applying causation to the universe abandons features found in observed causal cases, including occurrence within spacetime, interaction between efficient and material causes, and an affect-effect relation.

orphanFallback.rationale: The absence of these observed causal features independently supports a constructive scope objection to extrapolating ordinary causation beyond physical reality.

chunk-001:c008.proposition: Creation without efficient-material interaction would produce an effect without anything being affected, making transcendent causation less intelligible than restricting the causal principle to physical reality.

orphanFallback.rationale: The need for something to be affected provides an independent constructive account of why causation without preexisting material conditions carries a substantial conceptual cost.

chunk-001:c009.proposition: A universe that exists at every temporal point is not aptly described as popping into existence from nothing, so intuitions about objects newly appearing within time do not transfer to the cosmic boundary.

orphanFallback.rationale: The distinction between temporal exhaustiveness and appearance after an earlier absence independently undermines the analogy between the universe and ordinary objects beginning within time.

chunk-002:c002-03.proposition: Principles requiring causes only for non-initial things or for things beginning within spacetime can preserve ordinary causal regularity without adopting an unrestricted metaphysical causal principle.

orphanFallback.rationale: These narrower principles constitute a constructive alternative that explains ordinary regularity while withholding causal commitment about the initial boundary of spacetime.

chunk-002:c002-07.proposition: Allowing a special class of uncaused occurrences does not imply that unrelated events or intracosmic objects should occur uncaused, just as a possible exception for mental events would not predict arbitrary physical events.

orphanFallback.rationale: The possibility of class-restricted exceptions independently supplies a constructive reason why selective uncaused existence need not entail unrestricted spontaneous events or objects.

chunk-002:c002-08.proposition: A universe existing at every temporal point differs fundamentally from a universe appearing after an interval of empty time, and only the latter matches the rejected picture of a sudden uncaused appearance.

orphanFallback.rationale: This temporal distinction independently clarifies the con position by separating an always-temporally-present universe from an object that appears after an earlier period of nonexistence.

chunk-002:c002-09.proposition: Claiming that selective uncaused existence is inexplicable asserts that no explanation is possible, so the claimant bears the burden of supporting that stronger modal conclusion.

orphanFallback.rationale: As a constructive burden principle, the distinction between requesting an explanation and proving explanation impossible limits what follows from the absence of an immediately supplied account.
